newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cen.bank head seeks new IMF accord - paper.
newsitem.headline: Romania cen.bank head seeks new IMF accord - paper.

text.p: Central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu was quoted as saying on Tuesday that Romania hoped to lift the suspension of credits from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"The National Bank maintains a professional and reliable dialogue with the International Monetary Fund and a new accord could be concluded soon on this basis," Isarescu said in an interview with the daily newspaper Romania Libera.

Last December, Romania signed a $280 million loan accord with the IMF. But the Fund suspended disbursement of loan tranches earlier this year after expressing concern over restrictions on the local foreign exchange market.
Economists say Romania's chances of restoring IMF credits are much improved since reformists took power in parliamentary and presidential elections, ousting ex-Communists in power since 1989.

President Emil Constantinescu, elected at the weekend, is committed to a programme of faster economic reforms, mixing tight financial discipline with improved benefits to raise some of the lowest living standards in eastern Europe.
An accord with the IMF could consolidate and expand Romania's access to external financing sources, including international lenders, syndicated loans and bond markets, Isarescu said.

"What is essential for a new accord (with the IMF) is a programme of economic, monetary and budgetary policies, as well as restructuring," Isarescu told the paper. "It is the economic policy programme that will give credibility to Romania." -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest newsroom +401 614-6573
